subject: Throughput sizing follow-up & next steps (Finex)

Subject: Follow-up: throughput & latency details from today's call

Hi Rafael -- thanks for the call earlier. Quick recap from our side and a couple of asks so we can move forward with a sizing recommendation: 

- Primary use case: low-latency payment auth + fraud scoring endpoint. Requests come from our payment gateway and need synchronous responses.
- Expected steady-state: ~60 QPS across NA during business hours.
- Expected peak bursts: up to ~200 QPS (brief spikes, ~5-10min) during promotions.
- Typical request: user context + transaction metadata
- Average tokens: we exported a small sample (attached).

As next steps, can you confirm:
1) tokens/sec assumptions you need (prompt vs completion)?
2) concurrency assumptions and whether streaming is required for us to meet user experience goals?
3) any short-term test we can run to validate latency at peak?

I've attached Traffic_profile.csv (QPS by minute sample) and sample_prompts.txt. Happy to set up a short follow-up with our infra lead Priya if you need logs.

Thanks,
Alex
Alex Johnson
Head of Engineering, Finex Payments
alex.johnson@finexpay.com

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>

Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com, dylan.brooks@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 12 Mar 2026 18:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: throughput & latency details from today's call

Alex — thanks for the clear recap and the attachments. Short answers up front and then a proposed follow-up plan: 

1) Tokens/sec: we'll size against peak tokens/sec. Helpful if you can confirm average prompt tokens and average completion tokens from your sample; if not, we can assume conservative values for initial sizing (prompt 512 tokens, completion 128 tokens).
2) Concurrency / streaming: for synchronous payment auth we recommend streaming the first token for large completions to reduce perceived latency, but streaming isn't strictly required if completions stay <128 tokens. Concurrency-wise, we size for QPS and a headroom multiplier (x1.5) for spikes.
3) Test: we can run a short load test from our dedicated staging pool if you can provide a sample trace or allow IPs for a test harness.

Proposed next steps: 
- Marissa will put together a conservative throughput sheet (tokens/sec, GPU counts, baseline p95 estimates) and share a sizing template.
- If you can share a 1-hour traffic export (minute granularity) we will run quick calculations and confirm recommended configuration and cost estimate.
- Schedule a 30-min sizing sync next week to review numbers.

I'll let Marissa add the technical calc.

Regards,
Rafael Mendes
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@finexpay.com>, rafael.mendes@redwood.com
Cc: dylan.brooks@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 13 Mar 2026 09:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: throughput & latency details from today's call — preliminary sizing

Alex / Rafael — thanks, I pulled your attachments and sketched a conservative sizing model. Key assumptions and results below — please review and correct any assumption that doesn't match your traffic.

Assumptions (conservative):
- Avg prompt tokens (user context + metadata): 512 tokens
- Avg completion tokens (model output): 128 tokens
- Tokens per request: 640 tokens/request
- Steady-state QPS: 60
- Peak QPS: 200 (spikes up to ~10 minutes)
- Headroom multiplier for sizing: 1.5 (to cover short spikes and retries)
- Streaming: recommended for completions >64 tokens to improve perceived latency (first-byte streaming)

Sizing calc (tokens/sec basis):
- Steady-state tokens/sec = 60 QPS * 640 = 38,400 tokens/sec
- Peak tokens/sec = 200 QPS * 640 = 128,000 tokens/sec
- Sized tokens/sec with headroom = 128,000 * 1.5 = 192,000 tokens/sec

Rough capacity guidance (rounded):
- For steady-state: a small dedicated pool or shared hosted with caching could handle 38k t/s comfortably.
- For peaks: recommend a dedicated pool sized for ~200k t/s or a Dedicated + autoscale config with fast burst capacity to handle 10-min spikes.

Latency & concurrency notes:
- Latency SLO: if you need p95 first-byte <= 200ms for 512-token prompts, we recommend routing to a low-latency region and enabling streaming + shorter compilation kernels; exact numbers depend on model choice (gpt-like vs LLaMA family) and quantization.
- Concurrency: 200 QPS peak implies concurrent in-flight requests will vary with model latency; assuming avg server-side processing 300ms, concurrency ~= QPS * latency (in seconds) -> 200 * 0.3 = 60 concurrent slots. We size with ~150 concurrent capacity to allow headroom.

Next steps / ask from Finex: 
1) If possible, send a 1-hour minute-granularity export (CSV) of QPS (we can use your Traffic_profile.csv if that has minute buckets).
2) Confirm whether streaming first-byte is required for your UX — we assumed yes for completions >64 tokens.
3) If you can run a short sample replay (we can provide a test harness), we'll measure p50/p95 under a realistic token mix and provide a concrete GPU count + cost estimate.

I've attached a Redwood sizing template with the calculations and a column for you to paste actual token counts. Once you paste your real token distribution we will finalize recommended configs and provide a tight cost + latency estimate.

Proposed meeting: Thu 19 Mar 2026 11:00 AM PT — 30min sizing sync (let me know if that works).

Files attached: redwood-sizing-template.xlsx

Cheers,
Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
Attachment: redwood-sizing-template.xlsx (xlsx)
